A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaSeal framework and share most experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and appendix organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermarking measurements on DIV2K, COCO, and generated images, alongside transformation tests, adaptive-forgery demonstrations, efficiency measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a diffusion-regeneration attack demonstration in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Semantic caption extraction, ECDSA signing, QR encoding, DWT/INN embedding and extraction, and training losses remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions in Section 5 explain the existing procedure rather than introduce new components.

E1.justification: DIV2K, COCO, and Stable Diffusion image coverage is retained. Appendix C adds a distinct test scenario in which watermarked images undergo diffusion-based regeneration for watermark removal.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain HiDDeN, RivaGAN, WAM, and DwtDctSvd, with Stable Signature additionally included in the generated-image comparison. Newly cited attacks do not introduce comparative watermarking baselines.

E3.justification: Existing splits, resolutions, training settings, and metrics are unchanged. Appendix C introduces regeneration followed by decoding and attribution verification, with PSNR/SSIM measured against the original image; detailed attack hyperparameters are not supplied.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 11 examine watermark removal through regeneration and demonstrate an undecodable recovered signature. Existing editing, adaptive-forgery, payload-density, transformation, and noisy-layer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 preserve the same plus/minus reporting. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. Appendix C newly reports failed attribution after regeneration, with PSNR/SSIM of 23.23 dB/0.909 versus 35.58 dB/0.965 before the attack. These are added attack-condition outcomes, not changed benchmark scores.

T1.justification: v1's Definition 2, including its signing-oracle unforgeability game, is removed; v2 retains an informal appeal to digital-signature security. The probability expressions from v1 Section 5.4 survive in v2 Appendix A, so their relocation is not a new theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the broad 'first image attribution watermark' claim with a more restrained formulation and qualifies benign-transformation robustness as holding 'to a certain extent.' The principal method, attribution, and extraction claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses limited robustness and the risk that greater transformation tolerance increases misattribution, identifying selective robustness as unresolved. It also explains regeneration failure and characterizes Appendix A's analysis as design rationale rather than a formal security proof.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Architecture details, optimizer, loss weights, hardware, and documented transformation parameters otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion concerning recent forgery/removal attacks, fingerprinting, INN steganography and watermarking, and digital-signature security. These extend the existing research positioning; publication updates for previously cited works are not new references.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises the contribution list and selected explanations, moves and rewrites Section 5.4 as Appendix A, and adds acknowledgments. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds regeneration Figure 11, places existing Figures 8–9 side by side, updates plot labels and table highlighting, and revises title/author/header formatting. Existing appendix figures are relocated and renumbered rather than replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: The regeneration failure example and explicit robustness limitations improve transparency, while Appendix A clarifies that the retained analysis is not a security proof. The code-access link improves reproducibility information. Removing the formal unforgeability definition reduces specification detail, and the new attack evidence remains illustrative; with the core method and benchmark evidence unchanged, the net improvement is limited.
